A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical TGNN research. The main text, equations, four figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and can be matched. v2 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 contains mathematical definitions, constructive proofs, and illustrative graph counterexamples, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical, including its appendices. Its added checklist marks experimental results, settings, statistical significance, and compute resources as inapplicable.

M1.justification: The MPNN and three TGNN architectures, update rules, aggregation mechanisms, and time encoding remain unchanged. The revisions concern which logical formulas the existing constructions express.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. The illustrated temporal graphs are mathematical examples and counterexamples.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. The same TGNN classes are compared theoretically; added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, metrics, training budgets, sample sizes, or testing procedures. The added checklist supplies no evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or error studies. Revisions to formal counterexample arguments belong to T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. v2's checklist explicitly marks experimental statistical significance as inapplicable.

E6.justification: There are no empirical numerical results, rankings, or experimental qualitative findings in either version. Changes to mathematical expressiveness results are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Section 7 substantially revises the global-TGNN fragment L2: v1 places temporal operators directly inside a spatial diamond, whereas v2 requires temporal subformulas of the form Q◇ψ, with Q in {Y, P}. This changes the mathematical scope of v1 Theorem 6/v2 Theorem 11 and its Appendix B.6 argument. The separation witness also changes from ◇(c1 ∧ ◇Yc2) to ◇(c1 ∧ Y◇c2) in v1 Theorem 3/v2 Theorem 8 and Appendix B.3. These operator orders are not equivalent on evolving graphs.

C1.justification: The abstract tempers its claim of providing the first logical characterisations to providing the first results on logical expressiveness. The introduction and conclusion retain the same principal lower-bound and separation contributions.

C2.justification: Both versions explain expressiveness differences through the interaction of spatial and temporal information. Section 8 retains the same limitation: formal expressibility does not establish practical learnability. The checklist adds no substantive limitation or interpretation.

D1.justification: No implementation, hardware, training, or resource-access information is added or changed. The existing network and time2vec specifications remain; the checklist's code, data, and compute items provide no additional reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds four references covering bounded GNNs, global-readout GNNs, and standpoint temporal logic (v2 references 12, 13, 15, and 20). This modestly broadens the literature discussion while retaining the product-logic positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes local grammar and terminology edits, adjusts the abstract, updates affiliation and conference text, and adds funding acknowledgments and a checklist. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact; theorem renumbering does not represent newly added theorems.

P2.justification: The same four figures are retained without substantive redrawing, and neither version has tables. Caption references and page flow change, and the checklist is appended. Figure 3 retains the old theorem numbers despite renumbering in the surrounding text.

improvement.justification: The revised L2 operator order better matches historical-neighbour aggregation, and the corrected separation witness now matches Figure 2, improving the internal consistency of important arguments. The more cautious abstract also improves precision. These targeted gains are partly offset by stale theorem references in Figure 3 and retained checklist instructions; the framework and most proofs remain unchanged.
